column3: NASB follows the critical text without “named”; “sexual immorality” is rendered “immorality,” “pagans” is “Gentiles,” and it adds “does not exist.”
NASB follows the critical text (“removed”); “puffed up” is rendered “have become arrogant,” and the verse is a statement rather than a question.
NASB follows the critical text without “as”; it moves “as though I were present” to the end.
NASB follows the critical text without “Christ” in both places.
NASB reads “the Lord Jesus,” following manuscripts that have “Jesus”; it adds “I have decided” and “his.”
NASB follows the critical text without “therefore” and “for us”; it adds “in fact.”
NASB renders “so that we may celebrate” as “Let us therefore celebrate.”
NASB adds “my” and renders “the sexually immoral” as “immoral people.”
NASB follows the critical text; it adds “I did not … mean” and renders “you were obliged” as “you would have to.”
NASB follows the critical text (“now”); “designated” is rendered “so-called,” and “verbal abuser” is “reviler.”
NASB follows the critical text; it adds “the church.”
NASB follows the critical text (“judges,” “Remove”); the quotation is in capitals.
